notes: §1985:XIV.2.2.3 SR3: "Except for the INITIAL clause, the optional clauses may be written in any order." The grammar takes the clauses as cdClause+ in any order with INITIAL fixed in cdMode before INPUT or I-O; ReadClauses files each clause under its field whatever its position (refusing a clause written twice or of another format), and BuildArea lays the implicit description out from the CommunicationFormats table in §1985:XIV.2.2.4 GR2 and GR24 order, so the written order never moves a field. The witness runs Format 1 with four clauses out of print order and prints CD CLAUSES ACCEPTED. Probes at --std 85: (d) all eleven Format 1 clauses in reverse order over an X(87) redefinition, each named field moved to, printed AAAAAAAAAAAABBBBBBBBBBBBCCCCCCCCCCCCDDDDDDDDDDDD12345612345678SSSSSSSSSSSS1234EKK654321, positions 1-87 exactly as GR2 lays them; Format 3's six clauses reversed over an X(33) record printed 12345612345678TTTTTTTTTTTT1234EKK (GR24 order). (b) INPUT INITIAL (INITIAL after INPUT) refused COBOL5506; INITIAL after a clause refused COBOL0001; STATUS KEY written twice refused COBOL6169; a clause mixed with the series of data-names refused COBOL0001. (c) --std 2023 refuses the section (COBOL0902). (a, e, f) not reached: no variable data, file or arithmetic in a clause-order rule. Every refusal's text cites ISO/IEC 1989:2002 Annex A rather than the 1985 rule, the cross-cutting citation matter kb/Work PB4950 decides; the outcome is the one the rule requires.

next.reason: 1985: "Except for the INITIAL clause, the optional clauses may be written in any order."; 2023: "No communication description entry: no candidate comes from a clause holding the CD feature; the candidates cover only report, file, data and screen entries.". No 2023 clause holds the communication description entry. The clause-order candidates cover report, file, data and screen entries only, so the CD rule has no counterpart.
